questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Value of a Scalar
questions.problem:
If $kB=[\begin{aligned}8 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}]$,
where $B=[\begin{aligned}24 & -12 & 6\end{aligned}]$
and $k$ is a scalar, calculate the value of $k.$

$k=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
To express $kB,$ we multiply each entry of $B$ by $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}kB & =k[\begin{aligned}24 & -12 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}24k & -12k & 6k\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the above result equal to the matrix given for $kB$ in the problem statement:

$$
[\begin{aligned}24k & -12k & 6k\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}8 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

We can solve for $k$ by equating any two corresponding (nonzero) elements. Let's choose the rightmost elements, $6k$ and $2.$ Equating these elements, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}6k & =2 \\ k & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** We would still get the same result if we chose any other two corresponding (nonzero) elements.

$$

$$

canonical_examples.problem:
If $k {A} =
\left\lbrack
    	\matrix {
        	1 & 3 & 4 \
        	6 & 0 & -2
    	}
    	\right\rbrack,$
where ${A} =
\left\lbrack
    	\matrix {
        	2 & 6 & 8 \
        	12 & 0 & -4
    	}
    	\right\rbrack$
and $k$ is a scalar, calculate the value of $k.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To express $kA,$ we multiply each entry of $A$ by $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}kA & =k\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 8 \\ 12 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2k & 6k & 8k \\ 12k & 0 & -4k\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the above result equal to the matrix given for $kA$ in the problem statement:

$$
\left\lbrack
    	\matrix {
        	2k & 6k & 8k \
        	12k & 0 & -4k
    	}
    	\right\rbrack
=
\left\lbrack
    	\matrix {
        	1 & 3 & 4 \
        	6 & 0 & -2
    	}
    	\right\rbrack
$$

We can solve for $k$ by equating any two corresponding (nonzero) elements. Let's choose the top-left elements, $2k$ and $1.$ Equating these elements, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2k & =1 \\ k & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** We would still get the same result if we chose any other two corresponding (nonzero) elements.
